c.v: Dearborn Heights is ATLAW’s next-door city: about 61,000 people in two halves, a north end along Ford Road, Warren Avenue, and Joy Road that shares the east-side Arab American community with Dearborn, and a south end along Van Born, Pelham, and Beech Daly that borders Taylor and Allen Park, with Telegraph Road running through both halves (between the Rouge and Ford Road it passes through Dearborn) and Michigan Avenue crossing the middle. Its injuries follow the arterials: Telegraph’s signals and crossovers through both halves of the city, Ford Road’s retail stretch from the Southfield Freeway to Telegraph and beyond, Michigan Avenue’s industrial frontage, and the pedestrian crossings on Warren between the restaurants and the neighborhoods. Hines Drive, the county parkway along the Rouge, runs through the north end with its own crashes and park injuries. In 2024, Dearborn Heights recorded 1,251 traffic crashes, with 385 people injured and no traffic fatalities.

ATLAW’s office is at 3 Parklane Boulevard in Dearborn, a short drive from Dearborn Heights. In 13 years the firm has handled more than 10,000 cases and recovered more than $100 million for clients, many of them Dearborn Heights residents. This page explains what is particular about a Dearborn Heights injury claim: where the injuries happen, who the defendants usually are, which courts hear the cases, and the deadlines that end them. sections.heading: What is different about a Dearborn Heights claim

c.v: Dearborn Heights drivers carry a mix of insurance policies, and coverage limits can significantly affect recovery after a serious crash. A pain-and-suffering claim against the at-fault driver generally requires an injury meeting Michigan’s statutory threshold (MCL 500.3135). Recovery may depend on the driver’s insurance, available assets, and any uninsured or underinsured motorist coverage. Michigan’s default bodily-injury liability limits are $250,000 per person and $500,000 per accident, although lower limits may be selected. We review every policy in the household before we value a Dearborn Heights claim. See our

Warren, Joy, Cherry Hill, Van Born, Outer Drive, Beech Daly, Inkster, and Pelham fall under Wayne County or city jurisdiction depending on the segment; Hines Drive is maintained by Wayne County. A crash caused by a qualifying defect in the traveled roadway may implicate the highway exception to governmental immunity, MCL 691.1402. Signal malfunctions and sight obstructions require separate legal analysis.

Dearborn Heights Police and Fire, SMART buses on Telegraph, Ford Road, and Michigan Avenue, school buses from the Crestwood, Dearborn Heights District 7, Westwood, and Dearborn districts that serve parts of the city, and county road and parks vehicles are claims under the Governmental Tort Liability Act’s motor vehicle exception (MCL 691.1405). The 20th District and the Third Circuit.

Claims up to $25,000, including mini tort claims for vehicle damage (MCL 500.3135(3)(e), up to $3,000), are filed in the 20th District Court at 25637 Michigan Avenue in Dearborn Heights. Injury suits over $25,000 go to the Third Judicial Circuit Court at the Coleman A. Young Municipal Center in Detroit. Wrongful death cases may require estate proceedings in Wayne County Probate Court, while the lawsuit itself proceeds in the court with jurisdiction. Settlements involving minors require court approval under MCR 2.420.

Corewell Health Dearborn Hospital on Oakwood Boulevard and Garden City Hospital on Inkster Road serve injured Dearborn Heights residents; Henry Ford Medical Center–Fairlane, Corewell Health Taylor, and Detroit’s Level I trauma centers also provide care, depending on the injury and treatment needs.

Like Dearborn, Dearborn Heights’ north end is home to a large Arabic-speaking community. ATLAW can assist clients in Arabic and English, with additional language support available in French, Mandarin, Urdu, and Spanish.

faqs.question: Where is ATLAW’s office, and how far is it from Dearborn Heights?

answer.v: ATLAW’s office is at 3 Parklane Boulevard in Dearborn, a short drive from Dearborn Heights. Free surface parking is available.

faqs.question: Where are the crashes in Dearborn Heights?

answer.v: At the Telegraph signals and crossovers, on Ford Road from the Southfield Freeway to Inkster (including Ford at Mercury Drive and Ford at Telegraph), on Michigan Avenue, and at the Warren Avenue crossings. In 2024, Dearborn Heights recorded 1,251 traffic crashes, 385 people injured, and no traffic fatalities. Wayne County as a whole recorded 50,355 crashes, 16,458 injuries, and 177 deaths in 2024.

faqs.question: I was hit crossing Warren Avenue or Ford Road. Who pays?

answer.v: A pedestrian injured by a motor vehicle may qualify for no-fault benefits through an applicable personal or household auto policy. If no such coverage applies, the Michigan Assigned Claims Plan may provide benefits, subject to statutory eligibility and coverage rules (MCL 500.3114 and 500.3115). Your pain-and-suffering claim against the driver requires a threshold injury and depends on the driver’s coverage and your own UM/UIM. See our

faqs.question: I was hurt on Hines Drive or in Hines Park. Who do I claim against?

answer.v: For a crash with another driver, the driver, through no-fault and a threshold claim. For a road defect on Hines Drive, Wayne County, with written notice within 120 days. For an injury in the park itself, the county, subject to the recreational-use and governmental-immunity defenses that make park claims difficult.

faqs.question: Where would my Dearborn Heights injury case be filed?

answer.v: Claims up to $25,000, including mini tort claims, in the 20th District Court on Michigan Avenue in Dearborn Heights; injury suits over $25,000 in the Third Judicial Circuit Court in Detroit.

faqs.question: I was hurt because of a signal problem or pothole in Dearborn Heights. Who do I claim against?

answer.v: On Telegraph, Ford Road, or Michigan Avenue, a qualifying highway-defect claim against MDOT generally requires notice within 120 days, filed in the Court of Claims. On Warren, Joy, Cherry Hill, Van Born, Outer Drive, Beech Daly, Inkster, or Pelham, the responsible agency depends on the specific road segment and may be Wayne County or the City of Dearborn Heights. On a local street, the City of Dearborn Heights, with the same 120 days.

faqs.question: How much does it cost to hire you?

answer.v: Nothing up front, and no fee unless we recover money for you. Michigan caps contingency fees in personal injury cases at one-third of the recovery (MCR 8.121).
